# KalshiPaperSim

A **paper-trading competition platform for Kalshi prediction markets**, built on real captured
Kalshi data: real markets, real quotes, real order-book depth, real candlesticks, the real
quadratic fee formula, and the real reciprocal YES/NO pricing rule. Ten aggressive algorithmic
strategies with unique usernames compete over a one-year calendar; every result is **computed by a
deterministic replay engine** and every input is traceable to an official source.

<!-- AUTO:COUNTS-START (regenerated by scripts/render-docs.js — do not edit) -->
53 verified facts (27 documented, 13 captured from production, 1 negative/404 evidence, 9 derived by arithmetic, 3 unexplained observations) · 19 flagged irregularities · 10 strategies · 9 real markets · 61 daily candlesticks · 50 automated tests
<!-- AUTO:COUNTS-END -->

**Live:** [GitHub Pages build](https://buffedlizard55-lab.github.io/KalshiPaperSim/) (static, computes in your browser) ·
**Audit:** [VERIFICATION.md](VERIFICATION.md) · [IRREGULARITIES.md](IRREGULARITIES.md)

## The honesty contract

This repository was rebuilt after an audit found that its predecessor **invented data**. The rules
below are enforced by code and by tests, not by intention.

| Rule | How it is enforced |
| --- | --- |
| No price, quote, fee, market or series is invented | Every value lives in `src/verified-snapshot.js` / `src/verified-candles.js` with the URL it was captured from |
| No performance number is hard-coded | `validateStrategies()` rejects any strategy carrying a literal result; strategies expose executable `decide(ctx)` code only |
| An oversized order is never filled at a made-up price | `exhaustionPolicy: 'partial'` fills only depth that exists and reports the remainder as **unfilled** |
| Modelled data is labelled as modelled | `depthModel` / `source` on every book; the pill in the UI says REAL SNAPSHOT or SIMULATED |
| A strategy that never traded is not ranked | `LEADERBOARD_QUALIFICATION.minTrades = 1`; it is listed as *unranked* with the reason |
| Attribution must add up | `equityChange = realizedPnl + unrealizedPnl − feesPaid`, asserted per strategy (residual < $0.01) |
| Anything odd found in official data is flagged, not smoothed over | 19 entries in [IRREGULARITIES.md](IRREGULARITIES.md) |

What is **real**: market objects, series fee configs, order-book levels, 61 daily candlesticks,
exchange status, the historical cutoff, the fee formula and its published table.

What is **modelled** (and labelled): depth *behind* the quoted touch during a replay (Kalshi's
candlesticks carry no depth), the market-maker feed that moves prices when no API credentials are
configured, and the one-year calendar clock.

**How to read this table.** 2 of the 9 ranked entries finished ahead of their $100,000 starting capital —
best +3.38%, worst -56.28%. There is no +800% curve here,
and that is the honest outcome of replaying 61 daily periods of a deep out-of-the-money Nasdaq-100 contract
(YES closed between $0.06 and $0.28) under Kalshi's real quadratic fee schedule: the two
survivors are precisely the two designs that respect the fee asymmetry between buying YES cheaply and buying NO expensively.
The "Contracts NOT filled" column tells the other half of the story — aggressive sizing hits the wall of real liquidity, and the
engine reports the missed volume instead of inventing an execution price for it.

## The roster

All ten entries share one mandate, given by the competition rules: **highest return only**. None of
them carries a stop-loss, a position cap or a volatility target; that is a deliberate property of the
competition, not an oversight, and it is why several entries end the window down 40–56%.

## Run it

### Server mode (full features)

```bash
npm start                 # http://localhost:3000  (binds 0.0.0.0)
```

Nothing to install beyond Node 18+ — there are no dependencies. Optional environment variables:

| Variable | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | `3000` | HTTP port |
| `HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address |
| `KALSHI_API_KEY_ID` / `KALSHI_API_PRIVATE_KEY` | unset | Enables the **authenticated WebSocket relay**, so the feed carries real Kalshi ticks instead of modelled ones |
| `ALLOW_USER_CODE` | `false` | Server-side execution of user-submitted Strategy Lab code. Off by default; the Lab runs client-side either way |

### Static mode (GitHub Pages)

`npm run build` copies `index.html` and `src/` into `docs/`. Opening `docs/index.html` — or the
Pages URL — runs the whole app in the browser: it detects that no server is present, imports the
same modules directly, computes the competition locally and stores your year in `localStorage`.
Every number is identical to server mode because it is the same code.

## The seven tabs

| Tab | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Leaderboard** | Podium + full table, equity sparklines, per-strategy attribution bars, generated post-mortems, and the unranked block |
| **Strategies** | The ten entries: thesis, entry/sizing/exit rules, mandate, and computed results |
| **Markets & Depth** | Real captured markets, the reciprocal YES/NO ladder, and an order ticket that quotes fees and unfilled remainder *before* you commit |
| **1-Year Memory** | The 52-week calendar, market regimes, human registrations, and the full trade log — the dataset for future analysis |
| **Strategy Lab** | Write `decide(ctx)`, lint it, run it on the real candlesticks, and rank it against the roster |
| **Verification** | Every verified fact with its status and a clickable source |
| **Irregularities** | Everything that looked wrong in official data, with evidence and the action taken |

## Architecture

```
index.html            seven-tab shell
server.js             zero-dependency HTTP + WebSocket server, REST API, persistent store
build.js              copies the app into docs/ for GitHub Pages
scripts/render-docs.js regenerates VERIFICATION.md, IRREGULARITIES.md and README's AUTO blocks

src/kalshi-config.js      verified constants: endpoints, fee schedule, 11 price-level structures,
                          rate limits, auth spec, candle periods, status enums, fixed-point rules
src/kalshi-fees.js        the official fee engine (taker/maker, per-tier, round-trip estimates)
src/price-grid.js         tick resolution, snapping and fixed-point string formatting
src/verified-snapshot.js  real captured markets, series, order books, candlesticks, 404 evidence
src/verified-candles.js   61 daily bars in compact form + an expander checked against a verbatim bar
src/kalshi-api.js         wire parsing, reciprocity checks, normalization, live/proxy/snapshot client
src/kalshi-auth.js        RSA-PSS request signing (Node only)
src/simulation-engine.js  OrderBook (real depth, partial fills, market making) + PaperPortfolio
src/backtest-replay.js    the deterministic replay engine and equity-curve analytics
src/strategies.js         the ten executable strategies + self-validation
src/strategy-runner.js    competition runner (seeded, per-series fees, regime control)
src/analysis.js           attribution that reconciles, qualification rules, generated post-mortems
src/competition-memory.js the one-year store: calendar, participants, trade log, export/import
src/strategy-sandbox.js   lint + compile of user strategies, action sanitization
src/ws-lite.js            RFC 6455 frame codec and WebSocket server/client (no dependencies)
src/kalshi-ws.js          Kalshi subscribe/parse shapes, backoff, relay + upstream feed managers
src/verification-data.js  53 verified facts, 19 irregularities, 4 competition-site analyses
src/app.js                the browser controller (server mode + static mode)
src/ui.js / src/styles.css render helpers and the design system

test/simulation.test.js   50 tests: fees vs the official table, grids, reciprocity, capture
                          integrity, execution honesty, roster integrity, replay determinism,
                          attribution reconciliation, sandbox, memory, WebSocket codec, audit trail
test/ui-smoke.mjs         runs the whole UI against a DOM stub and asserts what it rendered
```

## REST API

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/health` | GET | Service, version, credential state |
| `/api/state` | GET · POST | The full one-year memory (or replace it) |
| `/api/run-competition` | POST | Deterministic replay; `{seed, regime, settleAtEnd, finalResult}` |
| `/api/leaderboard` | GET | Memory leaderboard + computed leaderboard + provenance |
| `/api/markets` | GET | Real captured markets |
| `/api/orderbook` | GET | Book for a ticker, with `depthModel` and mutation provenance |
| `/api/quote` | GET | Pre-trade quote: filled / unfilled / VWAP / slippage / official fee |
| `/api/trade` | POST | Execute a paper order for a registered participant |
| `/api/register` | POST | Register a human competitor (validated, collision-checked) |
| `/api/advance` | POST | Move the one-year calendar forward N weeks |
| `/api/settle` | POST | Resolve open positions at $1.00 / $0.00 |
| `/api/regimes` · `/api/regime` | GET · POST | List / apply a market-regime stress preset |
| `/api/backtest` | POST | Run user code server-side (disabled unless `ALLOW_USER_CODE=true`) |
| `/api/candlesticks` · `/api/verified` | GET | Captured candles / the audit ledger |
| `/api/export/json` · `/api/export/csv` | GET | The whole year as memory for future analysis |
| `/api/kalshi/*` | GET | Server-side proxy to the real API, falling back to the capture |
| `/ws/feed` | WS | Ticker feed: real relay when credentials exist, otherwise labelled SIMULATED |

## Fee engine

Kalshi's published formula, implemented exactly and checked against Kalshi's own table:

```
taker: fees = round up(M × 0.07   × C × P × (1 − P))
maker: fees = round up(M × 0.0175 × C × P × (1 − P))
round up = "rounds up such that the fee + positionCost is rounded to a centicent"
```

Two verified facts drive the results:

- **`KXBTCY` has `fee_multiplier: 0`** — the BTC series is genuinely fee-free. Confirmed twice:
  the live `GET /series/KXBTCY` capture *and* the PDF's Non-Standard Fees table.
- **Fees are asymmetric by side.** Buying YES at $0.12 costs ≈ 6.2% of the premium in fees; buying
  NO at $0.88 costs ≈ 0.8%. That single asymmetry decides which strategies survive the window.

Source: <https://kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf> (effective 2026-07-07).

## Tests

```bash
npm test          # 50 assertions groups against official documents and real captures
npm run test:ui   # renders the entire UI against a DOM stub and checks the output
npm run test:all  # both
```

The suite treats official documents as oracles: the fee table (21 rows), the RFC 6455 handshake
worked example, the documented price-level structures, and the verbatim candlestick bar. It also
asserts the properties that keep the simulation honest — no invented fills, reconciling attribution,
deterministic replays, unranked non-traders.

## Limitations and remaining work

**Limitations of what exists today**

1. **One replay window.** 61 daily bars exist for a single market (`KXNASDAQ100Y-…-T33000`), plus
   14-bar snapshots for two others. Kalshi's live history window is ~3 months, so a genuine
   one-year competition cannot be replayed from public data — the 52-week calendar is a clock, and
   the strategy results come from the 61 real periods we hold.
2. **Depth behind the touch is modelled.** Candlesticks carry no order book, so replay fills walk a
   ladder anchored on each bar's real bid/ask with modelled size behind it. Real fills would differ.
3. **Point-in-time data.** The captures are from 2026-09-17. Without API credentials the app never
   fetches live prices; with credentials, only the WebSocket relay goes live (browser CORS and the
   signed-handshake requirement prevent direct browser calls).
4. **No settlement outcome.** These contracts had not resolved at capture time, so positions are
   marked to the last real quote. `POST /api/settle` can resolve them at $1/$0 as a scenario.
5. **The sandbox is defense-in-depth, not a security boundary.** `lintSource` is a token/pattern
   scan and user code still runs in your own browser (or on your own server if you enable
   `ALLOW_USER_CODE`). Do not expose the server to untrusted users with that flag on.
6. **Single-process store.** The year lives in one JSON file under `data/store/` (git-ignored).
   There is no multi-user auth, no locking and no database.

**Suggested next work**

1. **Accumulate history daily.** A scheduled job that appends each day's candlesticks and order-book
   snapshots would grow a genuine multi-month dataset — the missing ingredient for a real one-year
   competition. `data/` is already the right home for it.
2. **Broaden the universe.** Capture more series (KXINXY, KXTSLA, KXFA, KXCPIYOY, KXBTCY) with
   full candle windows so strategies compete across markets instead of one.
3. **Real settlement tracking.** Poll `determined` / `finalized` statuses and settle positions at
   $1.00 / $0.00 automatically instead of by scenario.
4. **Authenticated relay in production.** With `KALSHI_API_KEY_ID` / `KALSHI_API_PRIVATE_KEY` the
   relay code path exists but has never been exercised against the live endpoint (no credentials
   were available during this build). It needs a live smoke test.
5. **Multi-market portfolio accounting.** Cross-market exposure, correlation and per-market caps
   would let the "highest return" mandate be compared more meaningfully.
6. **Headless browser test.** `test/ui-smoke.mjs` renders against a DOM stub; a Playwright run would
   also verify layout, the live WebSocket feed and the static-mode build.
7. **Regime sweep.** The five regime presets exist; a matrix run (10 strategies × 6 regimes × N seeds)
   would show which edges are structural and which are window-specific.
